dedupe_keys.name: openems open source energy management system

description: OpenEMS is an open-source, modular platform for energy management that monitors, controls and integrates energy storage with renewable sources and devices such as electric vehicle chargers, heat pumps and electrolysers, including time-of-use electricity tariffs. It is developed mainly by FENECON GmbH with a wide group of contributors led by Stefan Feilmeier, and the OpenEMS Association brings together universities, hardware makers, software firms and owners. The stack has three parts: OpenEMS Edge runs on site, talks to devices and executes control algorithms; OpenEMS UI is a real-time web and mobile interface; and OpenEMS Backend runs on a server to aggregate, monitor and control many Edge systems over the internet. Recent releases added apps for the German renewable energy act (avoiding feed-in at negative prices), ENTSO-E price use, many inverters, meters, wallboxes and heat pumps, and a second energy scheduler. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitHub and archived on Zenodo, under the Eclipse Public License 2.0 and the GNU AGPL 3.0 by component, at no cost; it is very active, with monthly releases (247 tags). Caveats: device support focuses on hardware sold in Europe. Simulation uses are testing local and site energy management, storage dispatch and flexibility.
